summary: David DiNardo walks through version 2 of Taxifi, the AI bookkeeping and tax platform he is building for Canadian small businesses. He shows the full flow on screen: signing up, connecting a bank, seeing profit and cash flow in real time, how transactions get categorized, asking the app for reports, and bringing in a human when the AI is not sure. He closes with what is planned for version 3.
takeaways: Bookkeeping is a compliance requirement, so the goal is to make it fast, easy and cost-effective rather than something an owner has to think about.
When the AI is fully confident, a transaction is categorized automatically. Anything less lands on a to-do list with a suggested category for the owner to confirm.
E-transfers need the owner's input once. After that the app remembers the payee and categorizes it on its own.
Owners can ask Taxifi plain questions, such as last month's income and expenses, and get the answer with a PDF.
AI on a platform only goes so far. Humans still do the reconciliations and filings, and a person verifies every file before it goes out.
Owners who do not want to connect a bank can upload or scan statements instead.
Version 3 is planned to read uploaded documents, such as amortization schedules, and split principal from interest automatically.
